carousels.title: Youngest of ten

captions.instagram:
I'm the youngest of ten children. Born and raised in Brooklyn, a first-generation American.

My parents gave us three values: togetherness, family and hard work. My father, Norman N. Jemal, was also my mentor. We worked together at our family discount store in Spanish Harlem.

Swipe for where those values show up in my story, and save the three-question check on the last slide.

#Brooklyn #FamilyBusiness #Entrepreneurship

Which value did your family pass down to you?
captions.facebook:
I'm the youngest of ten children, born and raised in Brooklyn, a first-generation American.

My parents gave us three values: togetherness, family and hard work. My father, Norman N. Jemal, was my mentor, and we worked together at our family discount store in Spanish Harlem. By 16, I had started four electronics and music stores of my own.

#Brooklyn #FamilyBusiness

What's one value your parents passed down that you still use?
captions.linkedin:
The values a family runs on can become the values a business runs on.

I'm the youngest of ten children, born and raised in Brooklyn, a first-generation American. My parents gave us three values: togetherness, family and hard work.

My father, Norman N. Jemal, was my mentor. We worked together at our family discount store in Spanish Harlem. By 16, I had started four electronics and music specialty stores. In 1976, my father opened the first Wiz on Fulton Street in downtown Brooklyn.

Three questions I'd put to any founder:
1. Who are you building with?
2. Who are you building for?
3. What are you learning by doing?

#FamilyBusiness #Leadership

Which value from your upbringing shows up most in how you work?

carousels.title: The 4 moves

captions.instagram:
In 1976, the first Wiz opened on one Fulton Street storefront in downtown Brooklyn. Today I lead JemRock Organization and BUILT®.

I think about the road between those two points as four moves: find the gap, build the brand, scale the system, play the long game.

Swipe for each move, then save the 4-question check for your own business.

#Entrepreneurship #Branding #SmallBusiness

Which of the four questions would you answer first?
captions.facebook:
One Brooklyn storefront in 1976. A housing technology company today.

Here's how I break that road into four moves: find the gap, build the brand, scale the system, play the long game. The last slide is a 4-question check you can run on any business.

#Entrepreneurship #SmallBusiness

Which move is hardest for your business right now?
captions.linkedin:
A good concept is only the first move. The other three decide whether it lasts.

How I think about it:
1. Find the gap: a need that isn't being served.
2. Build the brand: "Nobody Beats The Wiz" paired memorable naming with clear positioning.
3. Scale the system: as the chain grew, I built our own construction and prefabricated fixture company.
4. Play the long game: after the Wiz came waterfront revitalization and real estate, then JemRock Organization and BUILT®, which I presented at the United Nations.

The questions I'd ask any founder: What need isn't being served? Will people remember your name and your claim? Is it written down well enough to repeat? Where is your market going next?

#Leadership #Entrepreneurship

Which of these four moves does your company do best?

carousels.title: The math of the housing gap

captions.instagram:
Per JemRock research, the world needs 96,000 new homes a day. That's about 4,000 an hour, 67 a minute, more than one every second.

Behind that math are people. It's why our mission at JemRock is to change how the world produces housing. UN-Habitat counts 2.8 billion people without adequate housing.

Swipe for the full breakdown, and save the 4 questions to ask any housing number.

#AffordableHousing #Housing #ModularConstruction

Which number surprised you most?
captions.facebook:
More than one new home every second. That's the pace the world needs, per JemRock research: 96,000 homes a day.

UN-Habitat counts 2.8 billion people without adequate housing and more than 300 million who are homeless. At JemRock, our mission is to change how the world produces housing.

#AffordableHousing #Housing

Did you expect the number to be that high?
captions.linkedin:
Before you react to a housing number, ask who reported it and what it counts.

Per JemRock research, the global housing deficit is 155 million units, projected to reach 240 million by 2030. Keeping up means about 96,000 homes a day: more than one every second.

UN-Habitat counts 2.8 billion people without adequate housing, 1.1 billion in slums or informal settlements, and more than 300 million who are homeless.

Speed is part of the answer. McKinsey (2019) found modular construction can be 20-50% faster. Our design target for BUILT® is more than 50% faster timelines. That is a target, not a result yet.

Four questions for any housing number: Who reported it? What does it count? What year is it for? Is it a result or a target?

#Housing #ConstructionTech

Which question do you ask first?
